## Logistics

| | |
|---|---|
| **When & where** | Thursday, Oct 15, usual lecture time and room — the exam *is* the Week-8 lecture slot |
| **Format** | Written, on paper: ~20 questions of equal weight, roughly half multiple-choice, half open (hand computations and short explanations) |
| **Covers** | Weeks 1–7: everything in the lecture pages and labs, through GNNs II |
| **Aids** | None — closed book, no notes, no devices, no calculator; all arithmetic is pen-and-paper friendly |
| **Weight** | 15% of the course grade |
| **After** | Week-8 lab slot = exam debrief + [project kickoff](../labs/lab08.qmd); [HW2](../homeworks/hw2.qmd) releases the same day |

The **[sample exam](midterm-sample.qmd)** is a full-length rehearsal with
solutions — same length, same difficulty, same format, different questions. The
single best predictor of your midterm score is sitting it *cold*, in one timed
90-minute block, before reading any solution.

## What "ready" means, week by week

Each item below is something the exam can ask directly. Every one traces to a
lecture section or lab exercise — follow the links when a box won't tick.

**Week 1 · [Why graphs](../lectures/01-why-graphs.qmd).** Choose a representation
(directed/undirected, weighted, bipartite, heterogeneous) for a described system
and defend it; read an adjacency matrix or edge list; compute average degree and
density; explain why a random test split can leak when data points are connected.

**Week 2 · [Classical graph ML](../lectures/02-classical-graph-ml.qmd).** Compute
degree, closeness, betweenness, and clustering coefficient on a ~5-node graph by
hand; run 2–3 rounds of
[PageRank power iteration](../lectures/02-classical-graph-ml.qmd#alg-w02-pagerank)
(simplified, no teleport) and find the fixed point; explain teleport (spider
traps, dead ends); run
[WL color refinement](../lectures/02-classical-graph-ml.qmd#alg-w02-wl) on
~6-node graphs and state precisely what matching histograms
[do and do not prove](../lectures/02-classical-graph-ml.qmd#prp-wl); interpret
[modularity](../lectures/02-classical-graph-ml.qmd#def-modularity) and the idea
of the Louvain loop.

**Week 3 · [Embeddings](../lectures/03-embeddings.qmd).** Write the skip-gram
objective and explain
[negative sampling](../lectures/03-embeddings.qmd#def-w03-negsampling) term by
term (role of $k$, cost vs the full softmax, the
[shifted-PMI fixed point](../lectures/03-embeddings.qmd#prp-netmf) in one
sentence); explain node2vec's $p$ and $q$ and match a regime to what it
captures; name the [four walls](../lectures/03-embeddings.qmd#def-w03-transductive)
that motivate GNNs (transductive, no features, no parameter sharing,
$O(n)$ parameters); spot walk-based evaluation leaks.

**Week 4 · [Knowledge graphs](../lectures/04-knowledge-graphs.qmd).** Score
triples by hand for
[TransE and DistMult](../lectures/04-knowledge-graphs.qmd#def-w04-scoring);
prove one-line pattern results
([TransE can't do symmetry](../lectures/04-knowledge-graphs.qmd#prp-transe-sym);
[DistMult can't do asymmetry](../lectures/04-knowledge-graphs.qmd#prp-distmult-sym);
why [RotatE composes](../lectures/04-knowledge-graphs.qmd#prp-rotate)); compute
raw vs filtered rank on a scored candidate list
([the filtered-ranking algorithm](../lectures/04-knowledge-graphs.qmd#alg-w04-filtered-rank))
and justify filtering; state what a missing edge means under the open-world
assumption.

**Week 5 · [KG reasoning](../lectures/05-kg-reasoning.qmd).** Formalize a
multi-hop question as a
[path/conjunctive query](../lectures/05-kg-reasoning.qmd#def-w05-cq); explain
why [boxes](../lectures/05-kg-reasoning.qmd#def-w05-box) (regions) are the
right container for answer *sets* and what
[closure under intersection](../lectures/05-kg-reasoning.qmd#prp-closure) buys;
contrast [easy vs hard answers](../lectures/05-kg-reasoning.qmd#def-w05-easyhard)
in evaluation; say when vector-RAG fails and what
[graph traversal](../lectures/05-kg-reasoning.qmd#alg-w05-graphrag) adds.

**Week 6 · [GCN](../lectures/06-gcn.qmd).** Build $\hat A = \tilde
D^{-1/2}(A+I)\tilde D^{-1/2}$ for a tiny graph and propagate a feature vector one
step by hand ([the hand rule](../lectures/06-gcn.qmd#eq-w06-handrule)); explain
each symbol's job in the [GCN layer](../lectures/06-gcn.qmd#eq-w06-gcn); state
the [low-pass / oversmoothing story](../lectures/06-gcn.qmd#prp-lowpass) in
spectral terms; produce the
[uniform-features argument](../lectures/06-gcn.qmd#exm-limits) for why message
passing can't separate WL-equivalent graphs.

**Week 7 · [The design space](../lectures/07-gnn-design.qmd).** Fill the
[MSG/AGG/UPDATE template](../lectures/07-gnn-design.qmd#def-w07-template) for
GCN, SAGE, GAT, GIN; compute a SAGE, GIN, or GAT (softmax) update on given
numbers; fill the
[mean/max/sum confusion table](../lectures/07-gnn-design.qmd#prp-agg) for
one-hot multisets and say why GIN sums; state
[static attention](../lectures/07-gnn-design.qmd#prp-static) and the
[GATv2 fix](../lectures/07-gnn-design.qmd#eq-w07-gatv2); explain what residuals
repair at depth; recall the
[ablation discipline](../lectures/07-gnn-design.qmd#alg-w07-ablation) (one
factor, ≥3 seeds, error bars, claims cite cells).

## How to study (in order of payoff)

1. **Sit the [sample exam](midterm-sample.qmd) cold, timed.** Grade yourself with
   its rubric. Your wrong answers are your syllabus for the remaining days.
2. **Redo every lecture's "Check your understanding."** These self-checks were
   written as exam-style questions; each answer links the section that teaches it.
3. **Redo the hand-computation lab cells** (Lab 2 centralities/PageRank, Lab 6
   propagation, Lab 7 exercise 1) *on paper* — the exam versions differ only in
   numbers.
4. **Rebuild the two big tables from memory**: the
   [Week-4 relation-pattern cheat sheet](../lectures/04-knowledge-graphs.qmd#def-w04-pattern),
   and the
   [Week-7 template table](../lectures/07-gnn-design.qmd#def-w07-template)
   (model × MSG/AGG/UPDATE). Both are standing exam material.
5. Re-read the propositions you can't yet reprove — each proof on the exam, if
   asked, is at most three lines.

Questions before the exam go to the course forum — clarifications get pinned so
everyone sees the same answers. On the day: bring a pen; scratch space is on the
question paper itself.
